metadata.title: Elon Musk defends tweets in lawsuit alleging they caused Twitter stock to fall before acquisition

left: Elon Musk testified in a trial that his tweets criticizing Twitter during the 2022 acquisition were not intended to lower the company's stock price.
The lawsuit alleges that Musk made false statements about Twitter's spam or fake accounts to delay or reduce the buyout price, which caused the stock price to fall sharply.
center: On Wednesday, Elon Musk took the stand in a San Francisco federal trial where shareholders accuse him of misleading statements before his 2022 purchase of Twitter for $44 billion.
Elon Musk's tweets about bots included claims nearly 20% of Twitter accounts were `fake`, causing Twitter's stock to fall nearly 10% on May 13.

Plaintiffs' lawyer Aaron Arnzen argued Musk waived due diligence and mounted a spectacle to lower the stock, while Musk told jurors `If this was a trial on whether I've made stupid tweets, I'd say I'm guilty`.
The lawsuit claims Musk violated federal securities laws by making false public statements, with shareholders seeking billions in damages if the jury rules in their favor.
Beyond this case, Musk is scheduled for an Oakland trial next month and has testified about a Tesla $420-per-share deal years ago, along with disputes involving OpenAI.
right: Elon Musk testified that his social media posts during his acquisition of Twitter in 2022 were not intended to lower the company's purchase price or manipulate the market.
Musk stated his tweets were 'extremely literal' and reflected his immediate thoughts, without expecting Twitter's share price to drop as a result.
Twitter stockholders accuse Musk of misleading statements causing investment losses after he announced pulling out of the deal, seeking damages.
Musk's lawyer argued Musk sought the truth about bots on Twitter, while plaintiffs' counsel claimed Musk aimed to renegotiate or cancel the deal by publicly criticizing the company.
